Velocity checks against prior transactions and defined action on raised alarms are detection rules plus alert response, the reaction element of monitoring activities.
Mandatory reporting of fraud, embezzlement, hacking, fake sites and forged cards to the MOI hotline and QCB is contact with authorities under a legal obligation.
Tailorable rule-based detection with online authorisation decisioning and query capability, integrated with the acquiring system, is transaction-layer monitoring and alerting.

Fraud vulnerability assessments across branch/internet/ATM/phone channels borrow the vulnerability-assessment discipline, but ISO's clause concerns technical vulnerabilities in systems, not channel fraud exposure.
Analysing new products and processes for vulnerabilities before launch is the requirement to address security in projects and new initiatives from the outset.
Setting fraud loss limits and triggering a business review at 90 percent of the limit is quantitative financial risk appetite management; ISO 27002 contains no clause on loss thresholds.
Protecting cards, cheque books and internet passwords while couriered to customers is secure distribution of authentication information and protected physical transfer.
Transaction passwords, two-factor authentication, multi-channel payee registration, transaction limits and alerts are secure authentication features built into a public-facing application service.
Limiting information and transaction validation to employees who need to know is need-to-know information access restriction under the access control policy.
Due diligence before enrolling employees maps to background screening and vendor due diligence to supplier assessment; the customer KYC element has no ISO 27002 equivalent.
Requires a dedicated team accountable for physical infrastructure security, an allocation of defined security responsibility for the physical perimeter.

Continuous review of systems and controls to close gaps in the anti-fraud internal control framework resembles periodic compliance checking, but the framework itself is fraud governance rather than infosec.
Regular fraud awareness for staff and customers is awareness and education activity, though ISO's clause is aimed at personnel and interested parties rather than a customer base.
Defined channels for reporting suspicious transactions and behaviour, with detailed investigation of what is reported, mirrors event reporting followed by assessment and decision.
Publicised whistle-blowing and dispute/suspicion reporting mechanisms with thorough investigation are reporting channels feeding event assessment.
A dedicated email address, phone line and trained response team for fraud reports is establishing an identified point of contact for reporting, a preparedness measure.
Continuous training to build the fraud risk team's skills is competence-building education, though scoped to fraud investigation rather than information security.
Requiring the investigating team to report to the relevant internal authority and drive the case to closure is the response and closure discipline of incident handling.
Adopting computer forensics, forensic accounting and large-volume data analysis tooling is the forensic identification, collection and analysis of evidence.
Mandatory reporting of merchant-acquiring fraud to QCB is a regulator notification duty, expressed in ISO only as maintaining contact with authorities.
Allocates reporting duty to the acquirer in a shared ATM network and requires issuer cooperation on recovery; this is a payment-scheme operational rule with only a loose tie to authority reporting.
Obliges the bank to hand data and documents to police even when not the victim, i.e. cooperation with law enforcement and provision of evidence.
Ongoing fraud risk awareness aimed at customers; ISO's awareness clause extends to relevant interested parties but is written for personnel, so the fit is thematic only.
Fraud prevention training delivered to employees through various forums is a structured staff awareness and education programme.
Board and senior management commitment and resourcing for consumer education is management support for an awareness programme, but the audience is customers rather than personnel.
Maintaining customer cyber-security awareness and encouraging phishing reporting with remedial action combines awareness education with a security event reporting channel.
Ongoing multi-method customer education, including on the risk of sharing login credentials, is awareness delivery reinforcing the duty not to disclose authentication information.
Requires a defined security strategy covering confidentiality, integrity and availability of data and systems, which is the top-level information security policy.
Evaluating internet-system security needs and adopting only well-scrutinised or officially approved encryption algorithms is the cryptographic algorithm selection requirement.
Two-factor transaction-signing to authorise online banking transactions is strong authentication protecting an application service transaction.
Risk-based token mechanisms to authorise institutional and corporate transactions are secure authentication techniques chosen by risk of the application service.
Assuring customers that website login and transactions are protected and authenticated is the requirement to protect and give assurance over transactions in public-network application services.
Combines logical and physical access restriction to authorised staff with processing and transmission integrity controls over systems and data.
A monitoring system alerting on abnormal activity, transmission errors and unusual transactions with a defined action plan is anomaly monitoring with alert follow-up.
Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of the online banking system against MITM/man-in-the-browser attacks is technical vulnerability identification through security testing.
Tracking and planning capacity while maintaining high availability of online and supporting systems against DoS/DDoS is capacity management supported by redundancy.
Generic mandate for security measures on mobile online services and payments, i.e. security requirements for an application service consumed on user endpoint devices.
Risk assessment of mobile fraud scenarios feeding countermeasures is the requirement-derivation step for securing a mobile payment application service.
Protecting sensitive information used by mobile online services and payments addresses information held or processed on user endpoint devices, typically by encryption.
Educating customers on protecting their own devices from viruses and malicious software is awareness delivery specifically about malware protection.
Mandatory 3D Secure cardholder authentication with a dedicated enrolment process is a secure authentication mechanism for a payment application service.
Compliance with externally imposed card-scheme standards (PCI-DSS, PA-DSS, PCI-PTS/PIN) is meeting contractual and industry requirements and demonstrating conformance.
Annual reporting of PCI compliance status to the regulator is evidencing compliance with mandated requirements to a supervisory authority.
EMV chip storage of card data with DDA/CDA card authentication is a cryptographic strong-authentication mechanism for online and offline transactions.
Bare requirement that magnetic stripes be protected; the only ISO analogue is cryptographic protection of the stored card data, and the control gives no implementation detail.

PIN verification must be performed online by the issuer rather than a third-party processor, with regular security reviews of provider infrastructure, joining authentication design with supplier service review.
Undifferentiated requirement for security controls on payment card systems and networks; only maps generically to securing networks and the systems on them.
Activating a mailed payment card only on the customer's explicit instruction is verified activation of an issued credential before it becomes usable.
OTP-based two-factor authentication for card-not-present internet transactions is a secure authentication requirement.
Alerting cardholders when transactions exceed customer-set thresholds is threshold-based alerting, but the recipient is the customer rather than a security function.
Behavioural scoring and correlation to identify fraudulent activity is anomaly-based detection with event correlation, applied to card transactions.
Investigating transactions deviating from the cardholder's normal pattern and confirming with the cardholder before completion is anomaly alert triage and verification.

Anti-skimming detection, tamper-resistant encrypting PIN pads, specified CCTV coverage and escorted, logged vendor access to ATM internals combine physical monitoring, equipment protection and PIN encryption.
Regular messages teaching customers to inspect ATMs for skimmers and added fixtures is targeted awareness communication to service users.
Requires an explicit contractual prohibition on merchants storing swiped card data in clear text, a security clause imposed through the merchant agreement.
POS terminals must be tamper-evident and encrypt PIN entry and payment data end to end using TDES/AES per PCI-PED/PTS, i.e. mandated cryptographic controls from an external standard.
Card details must not appear on merchant or customer receipts and must be encoded, which is masking of sensitive data in output.
Cheques carrying account numbers, names and signatures must be held in a secure area, i.e. protection of records against unauthorised access using a secured facility.
Digitally signed cheques must be secured with cryptographic techniques per the bank's cryptography rules, a direct use-of-cryptography requirement.
KYC-aligned identification and registration of new customers is the identity proofing and registration step of the identity lifecycle, applied to customers rather than system users.
Core banking servers and infrastructure must be reliable and resilient and follow network management guidelines, i.e. redundancy of processing facilities on securely managed networks.
Core banking applications and databases must be secured per software and data security guidelines, i.e. application security requirements built on secure engineering principles.
Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of applications linked to core banking and its database is technical vulnerability management via security testing.
Core banking must follow the cryptographic and key management guidelines, which is the use-of-cryptography clause including key lifecycle management.
Bundles archiving of security events for later analysis and Qatari retention law, encryption of sensitive core database records, and RBAC-restricted access for identified personnel.
